blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) has defended its legal authority to issue Philippine visas, rejecting anew Ombudsman Jesus Crispin Remulla’s claim that such powers belong exclusively to immigration authorities under the Department of Justice (DOJ). In a statement on Sunday, the DFA said its authority to issue visas was expressly provided under the Administrative Code of 1987, and was not merely delegated by the DOJ. The department’s response followed remarks made by Remulla, a former justice secretary, on his program in dzRH, which questioned the DFA’s authority over visa issuance and raised concerns about its passport services.
